abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces Intent-Driven Architecture (IDA), a novel paradigm that fundamentally transforms how software systems respond to evolving requirements. Traditional software architectures struggle with rigidity when handling dynamic business needs, resulting in significant maintenance overhead. IDA separates business intentions from implementation details through a hierarchical abstraction model, enabling automatic architecture reconfiguration based on semantic interpretation of stakeholder intentions. We formalize the intention modeling framework using π-calculus extended with temporal operators, establishing theoretical foundations for architectural self-adaptation. A machine learning-based intention classifier was developed to map natural language requirements to architectural decisions. Empirical evaluation across twelve industrial software systems spanning e-commerce, healthcare, and financial domains demonstrates that IDA reduces architecture evolution effort by 47% compared to conventional approaches while improving system reliability metrics. The proposed paradigm shifts software architecture from reactive maintenance to proactive intention fulfillment, offering a new perspective for software practice in adaptive system design. This work contributes a formal framework, implementation guidelines, and empirical evidence supporting intention-centric software development as a viable paradigm for next-generation software engineering.

Accurate software effort estimation remains critical yet challenging in software project management. Existing COCOMO-based models and machine learning approaches suffer from limited adaptability to diverse development contexts. This paper presents Contextual Effort Calibration (CEC), a significantly improved effort estimation framework that incorporates contextual factors through multi-task learning. The proposed method extends the traditional COCOMO II model by introducing dynamic cost driver weighting based on project similarity and historical performance patterns. We analyzed 2,847 software projects from the ISBSG repository, identifying seventeen contextual dimensions that significantly impact estimation accuracy. The CEC framework employs a neural network architecture with shared layers for common estimation patterns and task-specific layers for domain adaptation. Experimental results demonstrate a Prediction Accuracy Improvement of 34.7% over baseline COCOMO II and 18.2% over state-of-the-art machine learning approaches in terms of MMRE. Furthermore, the calibrated models exhibit improved stability across different organizational scales and development methodologies. This work provides empirical evidence that contextual calibration substantially enhances estimation reliability, offering software practitioners a practical tool for improved project planning and resource allocation in software development.

This paper presents ArchForge, a novel integrated development environment designed for intention-centric software architecture design. Unlike conventional CASE tools that focus on diagrammatic representation, ArchForge embodies a paradigm shift toward executable architectural specifications. The system introduces Architecture Description as Code (ADaC), where architects express system structures using a domain-specific language that simultaneously serves as documentation and runtime configuration. The platform comprises four integrated components: the ArchDSL compiler for executable specification generation, the Intent Parser for requirement-to-architecture mapping, the Consistency Verifier for real-time architectural constraint validation, and the Deployer for automated infrastructure provisioning. ArchForge's unique contribution lies in its bidirectional synchronization between architectural specifications and deployed infrastructure, ensuring continuous alignment throughout the software lifecycle. We validated the system through a case study involving the migration of a legacy monolithic application to a microservices architecture, demonstrating a 62% reduction in architectural documentation maintenance effort. The platform has been adopted by three software organizations, with qualitative feedback indicating improved communication between architects and developers. ArchForge represents a new category of software tools that blurs the boundary between design and implementation, offering a fresh approach to software practice in modern development environments.

Test case prioritization techniques aim to enhance regression testing efficiency by ordering test cases based on their failure detection capability. Existing approaches such as total and additional statement coverage provide reasonable improvements but often fail to adapt to changing code characteristics in continuous integration environments. This paper presents Risk-Aware Test Prioritization (RATP), an enhanced system that significantly improves test case ordering through multi-factor risk assessment. RATP integrates code change magnitude, historical failure correlation, test execution time, and module dependency relationships into a unified prioritization algorithm. We implemented RATP as an open-source Jenkins plugin compatible with existing CI/CD pipelines, requiring minimal configuration overhead. The system processes test metadata continuously, updating prioritization weights based on recent build outcomes. Evaluation was conducted using six open-source Java projects with 15,000+ test cases over a six-month period, simulating realistic CI scenarios. Results indicate that RATP achieves 28% higher average percentage of faults detected (APFD) compared to coverage-based techniques and 41% reduction in time-to-failure-detection. The plugin has been downloaded over 2,000 times and adopted by four development teams. This work contributes a practical, production-ready solution that substantially enhances software testing efficiency while maintaining compatibility with established development workflows.
